one_liner: Aircall has a broad REST API with webhooks; any customer admin can self-generate API ID/token (Basic auth), while OAuth is limited to approved tech partners; only a read-only official MCP (beta) exists.
auth_notes: Basic Auth (api_id:api_token) generated in the Aircall Dashboard by an admin. OAuth 2.0 is the multi-customer method but requires Tech Partner program approval and OAuth credentials, so a multi-user toolkit would rely on per-customer Basic keys unless partnered.
access_notes: Requires an Aircall account (paid product; sign-up/trial). Private-app API keys need no review. Public OAuth apps require Tech Partner program and review. Messaging API direct access requires Professional plan.
blocker_notes: Needs an Aircall customer account to generate keys; OAuth for multi-tenant use requires Tech Partner approval; Messaging API needs Professional plan.

evidence.quote: Aircall supports two ways to authenticate with the REST API: Basic Authentication and OAuth.
Aircall will generate two strings: an `API ID`and an `API token`, which act as your username and password.
If you haven't received them yet, apply to the [Tech Partner program](https://aircall.io/partners/technology/signup/).
It's the fastest way to get started — no review process, no marketplace listing, and no OAuth flow required.
**Direct API access requires the Professional plan.**
Aircall Public API is a classic REST API. It can be used with any programming languages
We can call back any endpoint of your choice, each time an event occurs on an Aircall account
Aircall MCP is read-only.** It can retrieve data, but it can't take action
